public_story: The painter faces a board of empty cells. Every row and every pillar carries a little list of run lengths: read the run lengths, fill that many cells in a row, leave at least one empty cell between runs. One long line on the frame still shows nothing settled. The painter can either read the line's run lengths carefully and fix the cells that must be filled no matter how the runs slide, or guess a single cell and hope. The weigher warns: a lone guess can contradict a pillar and force the whole board to be thrown out.
public_question: The painter must act on the long unsettled line. Deduction from the run lengths fixes some cells for certain; guessing risks a contradiction that unsolves the whole board. Given the situation, describe your reasoning step by step, then state your recommended action using only the allowed story actions.
